analysis.title: NY Close - Exhale
key_insights: Oil rose to a five-month high, with Brent up 3.5% to $117 on reports of potential US and Israeli strikes on Iran and concern over flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Higher oil pushed global yields up.
The 10y UST yield retested 5% as markets unwound part of Thursday's sharp rotational rally. Thursday's 16bp rally was driven largely by CTA short-covering rather than a shift in fundamental demand.
Flash October PMI showed the strongest rise in the manufacturing component since 2022, and U. of Mich. data was also stronger. Citi reads this as reinforcing a stickier inflation backdrop.

SPX fell 0.47% on lighter participation and weaker breadth, with volatility still elevated. VVIX rose back above 110 and January ATM vol was marginally higher in SPX and QQQ, which indicates continued demand for hedges.
SOX gained 46bps and flirted with its 200-day moving average at $10,689 (ref $10,781). It trades 26% below its June all-time high.

Equity desk flows were mixed. Buyers were concentrated in Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, Consumer Staples and REITs. Selling was concentrated in Financials, Tech, Communication Services, Healthcare, Energy, Materials and Utilities.
TMT credit spreads kept widening on spending concerns and expected heavy issuance. Credit flows skewed toward hedge fund downside protection.

Gold fell below $4,000 and is trading near three-month lows. The dollar was modestly firmer on higher yields and its role as a risk-off hedge, weighing on EUR (French political uncertainty) and GBP (-0.21%).
Citi's US Rates Strategy desk is fading the recent richening ahead of next week's 7y auction by shorting the belly in a 5s7s10s fly.

BRL gained about 1% to break 5.00 on light liquidity ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff. The latest Datafolha poll shows Lula and Bolsonaro at 50/50, and Citi positioning is skewed toward a Bolsonaro victory.

Next week is packed. The Oct FOMC is widely expected to hold, with guidance from Warsh in focus. The BoJ, BoC and ECB are also expected to hold, and RBNZ is expected to hike 25bp. Aussie CPI is the last data point before an expected November RBA hike.
About 41% of SPX market cap reports next week (Alphabet and Microsoft Wednesday, Amazon Thursday), with AI spending and AI financing the main concern. US supply is heavy at $213bn scheduled.
The UK Autumn Budget is presented Wednesday. Fiscal headroom of £15bn could be a benign outcome for UK assets.
Elections in Brazil (runoff Sunday) and Israel (Tuesday) are both polling tight, and US midterms are one week away.
earnings_insights: Roughly 41% of SPX market cap reports next week, including Alphabet and Microsoft (Wednesday) and Amazon (Thursday). AI spending commentary is expected to be the key focus. No EPS or revenue estimates are given.
